袖.meaning: A farmer's rusty <part>weathervane</part> is stuck, so he ties the arm of an old shirt to it as a windsock. The <part>reason</part> it works: the empty cuff fills with wind and points the way it blows. Now the farm's best weather forecaster is a <kanji>sleeve</kanji>.
袖.on: He hangs an old <sound>shoe</sound> on the vane's other arm to balance it.
袖.kun: The cat on the <sound>so</sound>fa bats at the flapping cuff through the window until she topples off the <sound>de</sound>sk.

猟.meaning: On the first day of the season, a hunter crouches behind a <part>fence</part> with a <part>fishhook</part> on a stick. A cheeky deer sets off <part>fireworks</part> right behind him. He leaps over the fence, his hat lands on the deer's antlers, and the deer strolls off wearing it. So much for <kanji>game-hunting</kanji>.
猟.on: He spends the rest of the trip sulking at a cosy <sound>ryo</sound>kan.
猟.kun: For dinner the innkeeper serves him <sound>ca</sound>rp and a plate of <sound>ree</sound>f fish.

狩.meaning: A museum <part>guard</part> has lost the night key, so he ties a <part>fishhook</part> to a string and dangles it through every air vent, crack and statue's ear in the building. At 3 a.m. it snags something: the key, and a very old sandwich. It was a long <kanji>hunt</kanji>.
狩.on: He celebrates with a cup of tea and four lumps of <sound>su</sound>gar.
狩.kun: From the last vent he also fishes out a toy <sound>ca</sound>rp.

妊.meaning: A <part>woman</part> starts spinning wool on her grandmother's <part>spindle</part>, and every week the socks she knits get smaller: grown-up size, child size, then little ones no bigger than a thumb. Her friends see the pile of booties and grin. Nine months of knitting: a <kanji>pregnancy</kanji>.
妊.on: A <sound>nin</sound>ja quietly leaves extra wool on her doorstep every night.
妊.kun: Her husband plays the <sound>ha</sound>rp to the bump, and her friends cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'

缶.meaning: A magician claims he can fit a whole <part>mountain</part> into a <part>bucket</part>. He waves his wand, there's a loud clang, and the bucket shrinks into a shiny little cylinder with a ring pull. Open it up: snow, a goat and pine trees. A mountain in a <kanji>tin can</kanji>.
缶.on: He tops each one with a pink <sound>car</sound>nation and sells them at the fair.
缶.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp buys one as a present for his <sound>ma</sound>ma.

鈍.meaning: A cowboy ties his horse to the <part>hitching post</part> and sits down to lunch with his brand-new <part>gold</part> knife. He saws at his steak. He saws at the butter. Nothing gets cut. The horse eats his lunch while he's still sawing. Pretty, but <kanji>dull</kanji>.
鈍.on: His <sound>don</sound>key happily licks the butter off the useless blade.
鈍.kun: A <sound>nee</sound>dle is sharper, and so is a <sound>bu</sound>ll's horn.
